CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it.
--   5 BLOCKED            no reading covers the pair AND the source carries a
--                        processing_blocked_reason that says its text could not be obtained
--                        or read: nothing of it can be read, so the pair is not reading
--                        debt until the block clears.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- A recorded reading ALWAYS outranks a block: a reading of held bytes proves the block
-- lifted (migration 122 ranked BLOCKED above the readings and masked them). A reading
-- COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id (the
-- parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1 and
-- 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading recorded;
-- 3 wins over 4 because a full reading supersedes a partial one of the same source.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read": the
-- writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. It admits exactly the
-- processing_blocked_reason values whose CHECK comment (migration 091) names an obstacle to
-- the text: no-full-text, paywalled, no-doi, not-indexed, language. `no-quantified-claims`
-- and `superseded` are copies of typed facts (a recorded reading; superseded_by_ref_id) and
-- the writers refuse them by pointer. `out-of-scope` and `tier-not-required` say no text
-- was unobtainable, so they are treated as NULL (the source owes its reading) pending
-- owner question 8 of the round-2 adjudication.
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'no-doi', 'not-indexed', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id

REFUSING: add-source --processing-blocked-reason: processing_blocked_reason 'no-quantified-claims' is refused: a reading is recorded with `db.py record-scan --text-scope full`; the ledger derives READ-NOTHING-FOUND from the reading and the absence of a row, so the reason would be a copy (CLAUDE.md rule 5). usage: full_text.py [-h] --ref-id REF_ID --session SESSION
                    [--artefact ARTEFACT] [--dry-run]

Derive the WHOLE text of a source's held PDF or web page, registered under its ref_id.

WHY THIS EXISTS (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.3 step 1; tooling T1, owner approval D8,
2026-10-09). The scan contract reads every admitted source against the whole parameter
list, and a reading can only be as complete as the text it reads. Batch 23 extracted text
by hand from PDFs it held whole -- REF-01027's derived text covers 4 of its 79 pages -- and
nothing could say how much of a document a reading had actually seen. A reading recorded
as `full` over four pages would make the catalogue imply "no code sets a requirement"
where nobody read the code (the GAP-061 shape). This derives ALL pages, in the page-marker
form the batch 23 texts already use (`[PDF page N of M]`), so `db.py record-scan` can
COMPUTE pages read against pages held instead of being told.

IT IS NOT A SECOND COPY OF THE LOG'S MECHANISMS. Which files belong to a source is
`retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source`; the manifest line is `retrieval_log.record_file`
(kind `text-extraction`, the kind batch 23 used); decoding a web page is
`retrieval_log.decode_artefact`. The derived text carries the source's ref_id, so quotes
read from it verify SCOPED (`retrieval_log.locate_quote`) -- which is what lets
`observe-term` refuse a quote found only in some other source's bytes.

NO NETWORK. It reads bytes already persisted under retrieval-log/. A source with no held
PDF or HTML has nothing to derive from, and the reading is recorded as partial, fragment
or abstract (or the document is retrieved first, R10).

    when the source's own logged bibliographic payload states a page range.

    A `full` CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST WHAT THE DOCUMENT IS, and the deposit is the only
    derivable statement of that (`retrieval_log.payload_page_range`): a landing page is a

help="base_parameters.parameter_id — THE SUBJECT (owner 2026-08-26)")

                           "'absent' records that the source asserts NO value — which is "

    p_ax.add_argument("--claimed-value", dest="claimed_value")
    p_ax.add_argument("--claimed-unit", dest="claimed_unit")
    # REQUIRED, and this flag is the ONLY thing holding the verbatim guarantee.
    # Before migration 073 `parameter` was NOT NULL, so every row carried at least
    # the source's own phrase for what it measures. 073 retired that column (its
    # verbatim job belongs to observed_terms.surface_form) and left `claim_text`,
    # `source_section` and all 16 `loc_*` columns NULLABLE — so a happy-path row
    # could carry ZERO verbatim from the source it claims to have read. The schema
    # cannot be tightened without a compensating migration; the writer can, in one
    # line, and this is it. The guarantee is therefore the CLI's, not the schema's:
    # a row written by any other path can still carry none.
    p_ax.add_argument("--verbatim-exempt", dest="verbatim_exempt",
                      help="Reason this --claim-text cannot be verified against a "

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/skill_vocabulary_audit.py — every value a skill names must have a home.

WHY THIS EXISTS (CLAUDE.md rule 8; owner 2026-11-06: "ensure all terminologies and
vocabularies are correct"). A skill is a prose caller: it tells an operator which words to
type into a writer. Two walk-throughs of skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md (2026-11-06) found the
conflict mapper naming a column that no table has (`mode_s_trigger`) and population codes
the identity lens does not hold (`VIS`, `DBL`, `OFS`), and the connection skill naming
verdicts (`SUBSUMES`, `CONFLATED_VARIABLE`) with no typed home. An operator who follows
such a sentence writes prose into a free-text cell, or is refused by a writer the skill
said would accept the value -- either way the page downstream cannot join what was typed.

WHAT IT CHECKS. Every BACKTICKED token in a skill, command or agent file that is SHAPED like a
vocabulary value or an identifier (contains `_` or `-`, or is all capitals) must resolve to one
of the homes the repository holds, and to nothing else: a table, view, column, `table.column` or
CHECK vocabulary value (dbcore.check_values over every column) or a view's CASE literal; a
`db.py` verb (from `--help`) or flag (from the parser source); a registered check id; a
pipeline-contract stage or criterion id; an R-rule label (governance/research-contract.yaml); a
skill, command or agent stem; a tracked path or basename; an identity, ICF, access-need, slug,
term or gap id live in its registry; `sqlite_master` / `sqlite_sequence`; a placeholder (a token
carrying NNN/XXX/YYYY/<>); or a token the file defines in its own table. Everything else is
UNRESOLVED and printed with its file. Bare ALL-CAPS words in prose are not examined: only a
backticked token is a value the skill tells the operator to type.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A HOME. Strings the audit scripts, the writers or CLAUDE.md happen to
quote (their markers, dictionary keys, module-level names, environment variables), and the
registry's own keys. Harvesting them made `item_code`, `E-08`, `population_code` and `axis_code`
resolve, so the check could not go red on the retired item layer it exists to catch. The markers
the gates read out of note cells (`[UNVERIFIED-QUANT]`, `CO1-NOT-APPLICABLE`,
`NOTHING-IN-SCOPE`) are therefore reported wherever a skill backticks them. That is correct:
they are conventions the 2026-11-06 ruling on joined cells queues for typed columns, not
vocabulary.

WHAT WRONG THING REACHES THE GUIDEBOOK WITHOUT IT. An operator following a skill that names a
retired container or a column that does not exist writes the fact into a note cell, which no
later stage can join (the 2026-11-06 ruling on joined cells), or is refused by a writer the
skill said would accept the value. It reads the schema, `db.py --help`, the parser source and
the registries; nothing is curated here.

ADVISORY, with a per-file report: skills written before the vocabulary moved carry prior-
version tokens, and the remedy is a prose edit under rule 4, not an allow-list here. EXAMINED
is the number of tokens tested. Exit 0 when every token resolves, 1 otherwise, 2 when it
cannot run.

Usage: python3 scripts/audit/skill_vocabulary_audit.py [--paths skills .claude/commands ...]
"""

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--paths", nargs="*", default=list(DEFAULT_PATHS))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not DB_PATH.exists():
        print(f"skill_vocabulary_audit: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        known = homes(conn)
    finally:
        conn.close()
    files = []
    for p in args.paths:
        root = REPO / p
        files += sorted(f for f in root.rglob("*.md") if f.is_file() and not f.is_symlink())
    examined, unresolved = 0, {}
    texts = {f: re.sub(r"```.*?```", "", f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), flags=re.S)
             for f in files}                                     # fenced commands are shown, not named
    # A vocabulary one skill defines in its own table (a mode, a status) is nameable by another.
    own = set().union(*(defined_in(t) for t in texts.values())) if texts else set()
    for f in files:
        text = texts[f]
        toks = set()
        for t in TOKEN.findall(text):
            t = t.strip()
            if not SHAPED.match(t) or len(t) < 3 or PLACEHOLDER.search(t):
                continue
            if t.startswith("--") or "/" in t:
                continue
            if not (t.isupper() or "_" in t or "-" in t):
                continue
            toks.add(t)
        for t in sorted(toks):
            examined += 1
            if t in known or t in own:
                continue
            unresolved.setdefault(str(f.relative_to(REPO) if f.is_relative_to(REPO) else f), []).append(t)
    print("skill_vocabulary_audit — every value a skill, command or agent names resolves to a home")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {examined} token(s) across {len(files)} file(s)")
    if not unresolved:
        print("PASS: every token resolves to a CHECK value, a schema name, a verb, a flag, a check, a "
              "contract criterion, a rule label, a registry row or a file")
        return 0
    for path, toks in unresolved.items():
        print(f"  {path}: {', '.join(toks)}")
    n = sum(len(v) for v in unresolved.values())
    print(f"FAIL: {n} token(s) in {len(unresolved)} file(s) name a value, column or code the repository "
          f"holds nowhere. Correct the sentence (rule 4: prose is a caller), or give the value a typed "
          f"home first.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    18	between extractions via `relate-extraction` / `derive-extraction`.
    19	
    20	**Keyed on the parameter, not on a container.** The subject of a determination is a `base_parameters` row
    21	(owner 2026-08-26); the item layer is deleted (CLAUDE.md §7). Treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code you meet as prior-version
    22	content, never as a target. A connection points at parameters, slugs, identity-lens codes
    23	(`base_taxonomy_identity`), extractions, or a methodology, **one kind per column** (migration 120). Four of
    24	the five are foreign keys; `--methodology` names a methodological principle and is the one target kind with
    25	no table, so it is free text. The connection id is computed by the writer, never typed.
    26	
    27	## Two homes, and which holds what
    28	- **A typed edge between two extractions** is the strongest link: `extraction_relations` (`condition_on`,
    29	  `derived_from`, `delta_over`, `insufficient`, …) points from one figure to another row and can cross
    30	  parameters; across two *sources* it needs `--cross-source <reason>` or the writer refuses. When one parameter's figure is computed from or conditioned on another's, file the edge
    31	  (`derive-extraction`, `relate-extraction`); a `connections` row alone cannot be joined.
    32	- **A `connections` row** is the narrative index of a relationship. Its targets are typed rows in
    33	  `connection_targets` (`parameter_id`, `slug`, `identity_code`, `extraction_id`, `methodology`; exactly one set per
    34	  row), so a renamed or merged parameter cannot orphan a link and every target joins.
    35	
    36	## Modes
    37	| Mode | Trigger | Reads |
    38	|---|---|---|
    39	| `parameter` (default) | a determination written or revised | the parameter's live `specifications` row and its extractions |
    40	| `evidence` | new extractions, gap update | `source_value_extractions`, `gaps`, PENDING connections |
    41	| `external` | citation mining finished for a slug | T1–T2 forward citations in `evidence_sources` |
    42	| `category-crosstest` | a named cluster (parameters sharing a physical element, an envelope or a population; what a letter-category was) | every unordered pair in the cluster |
    43	
    44	`category-crosstest` is the exhaustive pass (`decisions/DR-2026-07-20-intra-category-cross-test.md`, ACCEPTED
    45	2026-07-21; "category" is now a named cluster of parameters): the other modes follow what an author thought to
    46	cross-reference, this one enumerates all pairs so none is skipped. A cluster has no table: name it in the GAP
    47	and in each connection's description. Per pair (per program) give one verdict, in words, because no column
    48	holds a verdict: the two are independent; one subsumes the other; they interact; they share a physical element
    49	under distinct programs; they are one variable conflated under two names; or they are in genuine conflict.
    50	Compare only within a measurement paradigm and device class (`measurement_paradigm`, `device_class`); a
    51	cross-paradigm pairing is a derivation, never an identity, and never a genuine conflict. Flag
    52	**cross-partition leakage** where a shared element or population links parameters across a cluster boundary.
    53	**Not built, and said so:** the DR's pair table (X6) and its hard gate on `stated` (X5). Until they exist a
    54	verdict has no typed home: "interact" and "shared element, distinct programs" are `connections` rows, a genuine
    55	conflict goes to `cross-population-conflict-mapper`, and the verdicts with no row (independent, subsumes,
    56	conflated) are named in a GAP for the cluster so the pass is not lost.
    57	
    58	---
    59	
    60	## Step 0 — Scope and dedup
    61	State the scope (a parameter, a slug or a cluster), what identifies it, and the mode. Load existing connections
    62	for the scope (`python3 scripts/db.py connections --status PENDING`, then join `connection_targets` on
    63	`parameter_id` or `slug` in a read-only query). A new connection with the same targets and `connection_type` as
    64	an existing one is a duplicate: `add-connection` refuses it, naming the existing id.
    65	
    66	## Step 1 — Read, by mode
    67	Read the live determination and every extraction for the parameter in full; for `evidence`, also open gaps
    68	(`db.py gaps --status OPEN`) and PENDING connections. For each extraction note its lens columns, so a population effect
    69	on a shared parameter is visible. For `external`, take T1–T2 sources from `evidence_sources`, follow forward citations,
    70	log mining with `db.py log-mining`; a cross-slug citation is a cross-parameter candidate.
    71	
    72	## Step 2 — Identify connections
    73	For each finding ask: does it imply a design relationship between two parameters, populations or methodological
    74	principles not already recorded?
    75	
    76	| Type (stored value) | Test |
    77	|---|---|
    78	| `CROSS-PARAMETER` | does evidence for parameter X constrain parameter Y? |
    79	| `CROSS-POPULATION` | does a finding for population A conflict with or reinforce one for B on the same parameter? |
    80	| `COMPOUND-INTERACTION` | would applying specifications X and Y to one person together give a non-additive result? |
    81	| `METHODOLOGY` | does it affect the guidebook's method? |
    82	
    83	Confidence is `connections.confidence`, read from the column's own CHECK (`HIGH`: direct evidence links the
    84	targets and the source says so; `MODERATE`: implied by reasoning or an evidence gap). A plausible relationship
    85	with no direct evidence is not a connection and the CHECK admits no value for it (migration 122): file it as a
    86	gap (`add-gap --category CR --priority P3 --description "speculative: …" --skill connection-discovery`).
    87	
    88	Route first: a relationship at MODERATE or above is a connection; an evidence or scope gap is a gap (`RP`,
    89	`AUDT` or `CONF`); a population conflict goes to `cross-population-conflict-mapper`; anything else is discarded.
    90	There is no connection-shaped gap category.
    91	
    92	## Step 3 — Log
    93	```bash
    94	GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH/guidebook.db" python3 scripts/db.py add-connection \
    95	  --confidence HIGH --connection-type CROSS-PARAMETER \
    96	  --filed-in <slug> --source-skill connection-discovery \
    97	  --description "<one sentence: the relationship, its mechanism, why it matters to a determination>" \
    98	  --parameter 3 --parameter 12 --session <session>
    99	```
   100	The id is computed by the writer (omit `--con-id`; a typed one must equal `next-id connections`). `--filed-in`
   101	is a topic slug (`slugs.slug`, a foreign key). Targets are flags, each repeatable and each validated against
   102	its table: `--parameter`, `--target-slug`, `--identity`, `--extraction`, `--methodology`. The type sets the
   103	arity the writer holds: `CROSS-PARAMETER` and `COMPOUND-INTERACTION` need two or more `--parameter` targets,
   104	`CROSS-POPULATION` two or more `--identity` targets, `METHODOLOGY` one `--methodology`; a type the CHECK
   105	admits for which the writer holds no arity rule is refused by name, never filed unchecked; a parameter target
   106	must be `active` (a merged or retired one is refused). Description bar: usable by the determination run
   107	without further lookup.
   108	Bad: "turning space and chair length are related". Good: "REF-xxxxx Table 2 gives a 1.35 m swept path for a
   109	powered chair; that exceeds the 1.2 m the turning-space figure assumes, so the turning figure needs its own row for
   110	that chair class."
   111	
   112	## Step 4 — Verify and hand on
   113	Count before and after: `python3 scripts/db.py connections --status PENDING` lists the rows (`--summary`
   114	groups them by confidence only), and the list should have grown by the number logged. Consumption: when a
   115	determination uses a connection, `db.py update-connection --con-id CON-NNNN --status CONSUMED --session …`
   116	(`--status` is `connections.status`, from the CHECK). A connection that reveals a conflict goes to
   117	`cross-population-conflict-mapper`; do not log the conflict here. `connections.opus_reviewed` exists and no
   118	verb sets it; do not claim a review that no row records.
   119	
   120	## Rules
   121	1. Never type a connection id: the writer computes it.
   122	2. HIGH confidence connections feed the determination run (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` stage).
   123	3. A relationship with no direct evidence is a CR gap, never a connection.
   124	4. No `[A-Z]-NN` target and no prefixed free-text target: use the typed flags.
   125	5. Use the CLI only; the archived registers (`gap_register.md`, `connection-register-active.md`, per-topic
   126	   `connections.md`) are not read or written.
   127	6. Feeds `cross-population-conflict-mapper`.

1	---
     2	name: cross-population-conflict-mapper
     3	description: >
     4	  Systematically identify and map where population-specific accessibility guidelines
     5	  produce opposing specifications when applied to the same space. Searches by
     6	  CONFLICT DOMAIN (environmental parameter) rather than population pair. Retrieves
     7	  resolution evidence from fragmented single-population literatures that do not
     8	  cross-reference each other. Outputs a conflict matrix with resolution status
     9	  and evidence quality. ALWAYS use this skill when: determining a parameter for a shared
    10	  space (Universal Mode or Tier 1); a determination run meets a parameter that more
    11	  than one population's evidence pulls in opposite directions; any
    12	  specification mentions "adjustable", "zoned", or "user-controlled" without documenting
    13	  which populations conflict. Trigger on: "cross-population conflict", "competing
    14	  access needs", "accommodation conflict", "which populations conflict here",
    15	  "do these specs oppose", "conflict matrix", "resolution evidence for conflict",
    16	  "opposing requirements", "conflicting disability needs". Phase 2B–3 skill.
    17	---
    18	
    19	**Model:** Sonnet-class (retrieval/collation) · Opus-class or above (resolution synthesis + best-practice determination)
    20	**Input:** Environmental parameter(s) (`base_parameters`), a determination under review, or a room type
    21	**Keyed on the parameter.** `conflicts.parameter_id` (migration 122) is the key and `add-conflict --parameter-id` is required; the domain label in the matrix below is prose that describes the parameter, not the key. The item layer is deleted (CLAUDE.md §7): treat any `[A-Z]-NN` code as prior-version content, never as a target. Population codes are `base_taxonomy_identity.identity_code`, and `add-conflict` **refuses** a `--pop-a` or `--pop-b` the table lacks (foreign keys, migration 121); the pair is unordered and the writer orders it. **The matrix below is prior-version content:** its population descriptors (`VIS`, `DBL`, `OFS`, `SENS`, `NEU`, `IntD`, `POTS`, `MCAS`, "fibro") are not identity codes, and most of its domains are not yet `base_parameters` rows. Derive the live codes (`select identity_code, display_name from base_taxonomy_identity`); choose the code whose name and description fit, and where none does, put the proposal to the owner. Never coin a code (OR-17). Which descriptors become codes, and whether the matrix stays as a seed list, is open owner question 1 of the 2026-11-06 round-2 adjudication.
    22	**Output:** Conflict domain matrix + resolution evidence register + unresolved gap flags
    23	**Chunk ceiling:** ≤3 conflict domains per run
    24	
    25	---
    26	
    27	## 1. Conflict Domains
    28	
    29	The finite set of environmental parameters where cross-population conflicts occur.
    30	Search by domain — not by population pair.
    31	
    32	| Domain | Parameter | Pop A need | Pop B need | Opposition |
    33	|---|---|---|---|---|
    34	| LIGHT-INT | Illuminance (lux) | DEM: bright circadian (≥300 lux task) | NDV/AUT, NEU, PAIN, OFS: dim, controllable (≤200 lux ambient) | Direct |
    35	| LIGHT-QUAL | Flicker, colour temp | NDV/AUT: no flicker, warm (≤3000K) | DEM: cool daylight simulation (≥4000K) | Direct |
    36	| VIS-COMPLEX | Signage density, pattern | DEM, IntD: high redundancy, pictograms, colour coding | NDV/SENS: minimal visual clutter, muted palette | Direct |
    37	| SPATIAL-OPEN | Sightlines, enclosure | DEAF: open, transparent, 360° visual reach | NDV/AUT: compartmentalised, enclosed, predictable | Direct |
    38	| ACOUSTIC-LVL | Background noise, amplification | DEAF: amplified speech, hearing loops, low reverberation | NDV/SENS, NEU: quiet, low stimulation, no amplification | Direct |
    39	| SURFACE-TEXT | Floor/path texture | VIS, DBL: tactile differentiation, detectable warnings | MOB: smooth traversal, minimal resistance | Partial (resolved: truncated dome sizing) |
    40	| MOVE-FREE | Autonomous movement | DEM: wandering, freedom of circulation | MOB (fall risk): supervised, contained paths | Partial |
    41	| CORRIDOR-W | Corridor/path width | DEAF: wide (≥2400 mm for signing pairs) | NDV/AUT: narrow (reduced sensory exposure) | Partial |
    42	| COLOUR-CONT | LRV contrast levels | VIS, DEM: high contrast (≥30 LRV diff) everywhere | NDV/SENS: muted, low contrast | Partial |
    43	| TEMP-RANGE | Temperature (°C) | OFS/POTS: cool (18–20°C); NEU/MS: cool (Uhthoff's) | PAIN/fibro: warm (22–24°C); MOB (spasticity): warm | Direct |
    44	| PREDICT | Spatial predictability | NDV/AUT, DEM: fixed layout, no reconfiguration | MOB: flexible, reconfigurable for equipment access | Tension |
    45	| FRAGRANCE | Chemical/olfactory | NDV/SENS, OFS/MCAS: zero fragrance | DEM (olfactory therapy): scented cues for orientation | Tension |
    46	
    47	---
    48	
    49	## 2. Execution Protocol
    50	
    51	### Step 1: Identify active domains
    52	
    53	From the input (determination, room type, or explicit domain list):
    54	- List all population codes the space must serve
    55	- For each domain in §1, check if ≥2 populations with opposing needs are present
    56	- Active domains = those with ≥1 opposition
    57	
    58	### Step 2: Search for resolution evidence
    59	
    60	For each active domain, search in this order:
    61	
    62	**Priority 1 — Existing project evidence:**
    63	- the parameter's extractions and live determination (`source_value_extractions`, `specifications`), read per lens column
    64	- SQLite `connections` table for PENDING connections: `python3 scripts/db.py connections --status PENDING`
    65	
    66	**Priority 2 — Aged care / dementia facility POEs:**
    67	Aged care populations co-occur DEM + MOB + VIS + DEAF by default.
    68	Search: `{domain parameter} dementia care facility evaluation conflict`
    69	
    70	**Priority 3 — Single-population design guidelines:**
    71	Retrieve opposing specifications from each population's guideline set.
    72	Key sources per population:
    73	- DEM: Dementia Services Development Centre (Stirling); HBN/HTM; Hogeweyk evaluations
    74	- DEAF: Gallaudet DeafSpace Guidelines (2010); PAS 6463:2022
    75	- NDV/AUT: ASPECTSS (Mostafa 2014); PAS 6463:2022; Enabling Spaces
    76	- VIS: RNIB guidance; ISO 21542; ADAAG detectable warnings
    77	- MOB: ISO 21542; BS 8300; ADAAG
    78	- OFS: limited — functional deficit research primary source
    79	- PAIN: limited — OT CPGs primary source
    80	
    81	**Priority 4 — Built project case studies:**
    82	Search: `{domain parameter} post-occupancy evaluation disability accommodation`
    83	Weight: dementia villages > neurodivergent housing > inclusive schools > public buildings
    84	
    85	### Step 3: Classify resolution status
    86	
    87	For each active conflict:
    88	
    89	| Status | Definition |
    90	|---|---|
    91	| RESOLVED-EVIDENCE | Published resolution with outcome data (e.g., truncated dome sizing) |
    92	| RESOLVED-CONSENSUS | Expert/standards consensus without outcome data (e.g., zoned lighting) |
    93	| PROPOSED | Resolution exists in guidelines but untested (e.g., adjustable everything) |
    94	| UNRESOLVED | No resolution found at population scale. Covers both "no resolution yet" and "irreconcilable here — requires individual co-design". Where it is the latter, say so in the CONF gap's description (what the OT assessment turns on); no column of `conflicts` holds the Person-Mode handoff |
    95	| CLOSED | Finished without an evidence resolution — the question was withdrawn, or infrastructure settled it |
    96	| DEFERRED | Deliberately not addressed this pass. Distinct from UNRESOLVED: nobody worked it |
    97	| ACTIVE | Live, in hand, not yet closed or resolved |
    98	| RETIRED | Removed from force without a successor |
    99	| SUPERSEDED | Replaced by a NAMED successor — distinct from RETIRED, which names none |
   100	
   101	### Step 4: Log to SQLite
   102	
   103	Do NOT write to `gap_register.md` or `connection-register.md` (both archived).
   104	All output goes to the tracking DB via db.py CLI.
   105	
   106	**For each conflict (all statuses):** log to the `conflicts` table:
   107	
   108	```bash
   109	# Get next CONF-ID
   110	python3 scripts/db.py next-id conflicts
   111	
   112	# Log conflict. The writer orders the pair; the id is computed when --conflict-id is omitted.
   113	python3 scripts/db.py add-conflict \
   114	  --parameter-id [base_parameters.parameter_id, active] \
   115	  --domain [the domain label, prose] \
   116	  --pop-a [identity_code] --pop-b [identity_code] \
   117	  --status [conflicts.status, from the CHECK: python3 scripts/db.py add-conflict --help] \
   118	  --resolution "[mechanism if resolved]" \
   119	  --evidence "[source citation if resolved]" \
   120	  --session [session-name]
   121	```
   122	One conflict per (parameter, pair): a second is refused, naming the first (`update-conflict` changes it).
   123	`update-conflict --gap-id` and `--status` are checked the same way; an unknown gap or conflict is refused by
   124	name. `python3 scripts/db.py conflicts --parameter-id N` reads the key back.
   125	
   126	**For UNRESOLVED conflicts only:** also log a gap, then link:
   127	
   128	```bash
   129	# Log gap first
   130	python3 scripts/db.py add-gap \
   131	  --category CONF \
   132	  --priority P1 \
   133	  --description "[domain]: [pop_a] vs [pop_b] — [why unresolved, what research is needed]" \
   134	  --skill cross-population-conflict-mapper \
   135	  --section "parameter [parameter_id]" \
   136	  --session [session-name]
   137	
   138	# Then update the conflict with gap_id (use GAP-NNN returned above)
   139	python3 scripts/db.py update-conflict \
   140	  --conflict-id CONF-XXXX \
   141	  --gap-id GAP-NNN \
   142	  --session [session-name]
   143	```
   144	
   145	**For RESOLVED conflicts:** no gap needed. The `conflicts` table record is the full output.
   146	
   147	**For multi-run sessions (>3 active domains):** the wrapper re-invokes conflict-mapper
   148	with already-resolved domains as context to skip. Query before each run:
   149	
   150	```bash
   151	python3 scripts/db.py conflicts --domain [domain] --summary
   152	```
   153	
   154	### Step 5: Output conflict matrix (inline)
   155	
   156	```markdown
   157	## Cross-Population Conflict Matrix — [scope]
   158	**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
   159	**Space / parameter:** [identifier, parameter_id]
   160	**Populations served:** [codes]
   161	
   162	### Active Conflicts
   163	
   164	| Domain | Pop A | Pop B | A spec | B spec | Resolution | Status | Evidence |
   165	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   166	| | | | | | | | ● ◐ ○ |
   167	
   168	### Resolution Evidence Register
   169	
   170	For each RESOLVED or PROPOSED conflict:
   171	- Source(s) with citation
   172	- Resolution mechanism
   173	- Outcome data (if any)
   174	- Guidebook implication (Universal Mode default, Tier 1 range, Tier 2 requirement)
   175	- CONF-ID logged
   176	
   177	### Unresolved Conflicts
   178	
   179	For each UNRESOLVED conflict:
   180	- CONF-ID (tracking DB)
   181	- GAP-ID (tracking DB, category CONF)
   182	- Populations affected
   183	- Specification implication
   184	- Research needed
   185	```
   186	
   187	---
   188	
   189	## 3. Resolution Patterns
   190	
   191	Known resolution archetypes (apply where evidence supports):
   192	
   193	| Pattern | Mechanism | Applicable when |
   194	|---|---|---|
   195	| **Zoning** | Spatial separation of conflicting parameters | Space is large enough to differentiate zones |
   196	| **Adjustable** | User-controlled parameter | Individual can operate controls; not DEM or IntD without support |
   197	| **Temporal** | Time-based alternation | Populations use space at different times |
   198	| **Graduated** | Transition zones between opposing states | Adjacent spaces with gradual parameter change |
   199	| **Layered** | Multiple modalities serving same function | Information via visual + tactile + auditory redundantly |
   200	| **Tier escalation** | Irreconcilable at Universal Mode; resolved at Tier 1–2 | Populations identified; co-design available |
   201	| **Dimensional** | Parameter optimised at intersection of acceptable ranges | Ranges overlap even if optima differ |
   202	
   203	**CRITICAL:** "Adjustable" is not a universal resolution. It fails when:
   204	- The user cannot operate controls (DEM late stage, IntD without support)
   205	- The parameter is shared ambient (you cannot dim lights for one person in an open room)
   206	- Adjustment requires disclosure of disability
   207	
   208	---
   209	
   210	## 4. Interdependencies
   211	
   212	**Feeds FROM:**
   213	- the determination run (a parameter whose evidence is population-contested)
   214	- `connection-discovery` (cross-population tensions discovered — replaces connection-scout)
   215	- `content-gap-analyzer` (population coverage revealing conflict)
   216	- `multilingual-research` / `functional-deficit-researcher` (population-specific evidence)
   217	
   218	**Feeds INTO:**
   219	- the determination run (`assess_cell.py`): a `contested` direction and the conflict matrix decide how a spread is shown
   220	- SQLite `conflicts` table (all conflicts via `db.py add-conflict`)
   221	- SQLite `gaps` table (UNRESOLVED only via `db.py add-gap --category CONF`)
   222	
   223	**Do NOT write to:**
   224	- `gap_register.md` (archived — use `db.py add-gap`)
   225	- `connection-register.md` (archived — use `db.py add-conflict`)
   226	- `references/connection-register-active.md` (archived)
   227	
   228	**Preceded by:** population-specific extractions for the parameter
   229	**Followed by:** the determination. Where the conflict is irreducible, `set-parameter-direction --direction contested` records it, but the writer requires `--ref-id`, one admitted source holding an extraction for the parameter; whether a contested direction takes one source or one per side is open owner question 7 of the 2026-11-06 round-2 adjudication
   230	
   231	---
   232	
   233	## 5. Model Assignment
   234	
   235	- **Sonnet:** All retrieval, collation, search, and matrix assembly
   236	- **Opus:** Resolution synthesis — determining whether a proposed resolution genuinely serves both populations or merely privileges one. Opus adjudicates when "adjustable" is a real resolution vs. a handwave. All `Resolution` column content in the conflict matrix requires Opus determination.
   237	
   238	---
   239	
   240	## 6. Constraints
   241	
   242	1. Never assume "adjustable" resolves a conflict without evidence that both populations can operate the adjustment
   243	2. Never delete a conflict because one population is smaller — all populations have equal standing per CRPD Art. 4.3
   244	3. Always check whether a proposed resolution for Pop A creates a NEW conflict for Pop C
   245	4. SURFACE-TEXT (VIS ↔ MOB) is the only domain with a fully evidence-based resolution (truncated dome sizing per JIS/ISO). All other domains have weaker evidence.
   246	5. Dementia village literature is the richest source for cross-population conflict evidence because residents co-occur DEM + MOB + VIS + DEAF
   247	6. Do not search by population pair (55 pairs). Search by conflict domain (12 domains).

1	---
     2	name: citation-miner
     3	description: >
     4	  Backward and forward citation mining for confirmed Tier 1–3 sources in the guidebook
     5	  evidence base. Runs in two modes: INLINE (triggered automatically by research skills
     6	  when a source is confirmed) and BATCH (standalone pass over all unmined sources in a
     7	  slug or globally). Depth-1 only — mine references of each source but never recurse
     8	  into discovered sources within the same session. Tracks all mining in SQLite via
     9	  db.py CLI. Produces bibliography-ready output. ALWAYS use when asked to: mine citations,
    10	  find related sources, trace citation networks, expand evidence base, generate bibliography.
    11	  Trigger on: "citation mining", "mine references", "cited by", "backward citations",
    12	  "forward citations", "expand evidence base", "bibliography", "unmined sources".
    13	---
    14	
    15	**Model:** Sonnet-class + web search
    16	**Connectors:** PubMed (required), Scholar Gateway (preferred for forward), Consensus (optional). CrossRef via web_fetch acceptable for backward when PubMed lacks the record. Activate for mining.
    17	**SQLite:** `data/guidebook.db` via `scripts/db.py`
    18	
    19	---
    20	
    21	## 0. Connector availability (read BEFORE mining)
    22	
    23	Before any mining pass, probe connector availability:
    24	
    25	- **PubMed** — required for verification. If unavailable, ABORT the mining pass and log `[GAP — PubMed connector unavailable]`. Do NOT proceed with web-search-only verification (high fabrication risk per GAP-278).
    26	- **Semantic Scholar Graph API** (via `web_fetch` to `api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:{doi}/citations`) — **preferred for forward mining.** This is a genuine citation-graph "cited by" endpoint, public, no auth required. Use it as the default forward-mining method for any DOI-bearing anchor.
    27	- **Scholar Gateway** — its `semanticSearch` tool is topical/semantic passage retrieval, **not a citation graph**. It does not reliably return actual citing papers (confirmed empirically 2026-07-20 — spot-checked results were topically similar but did not verifiably cite the anchor; see DR-2026-07-20-citation-mining-methodology-corrections.md). **Do not use it for forward mining.** It remains useful as a supplementary topic-context search, same caveats as PubMed `find_related_articles` below.
    28	  If neither Semantic Scholar nor Scholar Gateway is reachable, mark `forward = 0` and populate `deferred_reason` with `"no citation-graph connector available — forward mining DEFERRED"`. **Do NOT substitute PubMed topic search for forward mining** — that is the topic-evidence vs claim-evidence anti-pattern PI standing rule #7 fights. PubMed `find_related_articles` is word-weighted similarity, not actual citers; it is not a forward-mining substitute.
    29	- **Consensus** — optional supplement for backward mining when CrossRef ref list is empty (e.g., conference abstracts).

It only requires the source document itself, read for its own reference list. This works identically regardless of language — see §2 non-DOI sub-protocol. Do not mark a non-DOI source `backward = 0`/deferred without first fetching the actual document.

   178	## 2. Mining Protocol
   179	
   180	### Backward Mining (reference list)
   181	
   182	**DOI-bearing sources:**
   183	1. Retrieve reference list via DOI → CrossRef (preferred), PubMed, or Semantic Scholar
   184	2. Filter for relevance (§3)
   185	3. For each relevant reference:
   186	   - Verify existence (CrossRef record / PubMed / Semantic Scholar lookup)
   187	   - Classify evidence tier
   188	   - Check if already in evidence_sources (dedup by DOI, case-insensitive)
   189	   - If new: INSERT into evidence_sources + source_slug_links
   190	   - discovery_method field: `backward_from:{local_ref_id}`
   191	
   192	**Non-DOI sources (grey literature, standards, government/NGO documents — non-English or otherwise):**
   193	Backward mining is **not blocked by the absence of a DOI**. It requires only the source document itself:
   194	1. Fetch the source's URL. **If the URL resolves to an organisation homepage, product page, or other non-document landing page — browse the site** (publications/reports/research sections) before concluding there is nothing to mine. A landing page means you're one click from the real document, not that it doesn't exist. Confirmed this recovers real bibliographies in the majority of cases where it was tried (see DR-2026-07-20).
   195	2. Fetch the actual document (report, handbook, guideline PDF, etc.) and read its own reference list / cited-sources section, in whatever language it's written. This is language-agnostic — a document's own citations are just as extractable in Norwegian or Japanese as in English.
   196	   - If `web_fetch`'s markdown conversion fails on a binary PDF (returns a "binary content saved to..." message), download it directly (`curl`) and extract text locally with `pdfminer.six` or `pypdf`. If the sandbox's `cryptography`/`cffi` binding is broken (a `ModuleNotFoundError: _cffi_backend` / pyo3 panic), `pip install --force-reinstall cffi` resolves it.
   197	3. Filter for relevance (§3), verify each candidate against whatever record exists for it (CrossRef if it later turns out to have a DOI; otherwise the citing document itself, plus one independent corroborating source where feasible — e.g. a web search confirming the cited report's real authorship/publisher), classify tier, dedup, insert.
   198	4. If the document genuinely has no reference list of its own (a practice checklist, a statutory text, a product page) — that's a legitimate NULL RESULT once actually verified by fetching it, not a deferral. Deferral is for documents you could not access (paywall, 403, genuinely no mirror found), not for documents you haven't tried to fetch yet.
   199	5. **Do not default `evidence_type` to `grey` because a source is non-English or non-DOI.** Grey literature is a publication-type classification (informally published, non-peer-reviewed), independent of language. Check the actual venue — a journal article, monograph, or dissertation in any language is not grey literature just because it isn't in CrossRef. Verify the publisher/journal/institution before assigning `evidence_type`.
   200	
   201	### Forward Mining (cited by)
   202	1. Semantic Scholar Graph API `citations` endpoint for the anchor's DOI (preferred — see §0). Scholar Gateway `semanticSearch` is not a substitute (topical, not citation-graph).
   203	2. Filter for relevance (§3)
   204	3. For each relevant citing paper: same protocol as backward, discovery_method: `forward_from:{local_ref_id}`
   205	4. Non-DOI anchors generally cannot be forward-mined (no index to query "who cites this non-indexed document") — mark `forward` DEFERRED with that reason unless a citing relationship is found incidentally (e.g. a later document in the same domestic literature that names it).

That makes the source invisible to any future language-prioritized query, silently defeating the point of ever running a non-English-focused pass. Use `native_title_verified` when you've read the actual title/text in that language; `journal_family_inference` when inferring from publishing in the same venue as a confirmed-language source (lower confidence — say so); `citing_document_language` when extracted from a bibliography written in that language.

   335	## 6. Depth-1 Rule (hard constraint)
   336	
   337	Mine references OF the source ✓ · Mine citations OF the source ✓ · Record new sources ✓
   338	Mine references of discovered sources ✗ NEVER · Mine citations of discovered sources ✗ NEVER
   339	
   340	**Why (corrected 2026-07-20 — see DR-2026-07-20-citation-mining-methodology-corrections.md):**
   341	Not fabrication risk — a discovery at hop 3 is exactly as verifiable against a real connector as one at hop 1, as long as it's actually checked. The real reasons are:
   342	- **Branching factor.** Backward + forward mining of 10 anchors in one pass produced 62 new candidate sources. Recursing into those at the same rate compounds geometrically per hop, not incrementally.
   343	- **Relevance drift.** Each hop away from the original anchor weakens the link between "real, verified paper" and "actually relevant evidence for the claim this slug needs" — the project's topic-evidence-vs-claim-evidence anti-pattern (rule #7), which gets worse with distance, not better.
   344	
   345	Depth-1 is the boundary where verification, relevance, and (where applicable) language focus stay tractable together. Going deeper is a real option for a narrowly-scoped, explicitly-approved pilot — not a default.

   348	
   349	## 6a. Citation-mining is not a substitute for multilingual-research (corrected 2026-07-20)
   350	
   351	The DOI-connector half of this skill (CrossRef backward, Semantic Scholar forward) is **structurally English-dominant**, independent of where you start: researchers worldwide disproportionately publish their DOI-indexed, internationally-discoverable work in English specifically so it gets picked up by these indexes. Running this skill's connector-based mining on a non-English-tagged anchor will mostly surface English discoveries — not because the technique is broken, but because that's what the index looks like.
   352	
   353	This does **not** mean citation-mining can't produce non-English discoveries — §2's non-DOI sub-protocol (fetch the actual document, read its own citations) is fully language-agnostic and works fine, demonstrated repeatedly 2026-07-20. But it means:
   354	- Don't expect the automated connector path to do non-English discovery for you.
   355	- For genuinely new non-English coverage (not just mining what's already in the DB), `multilingual-research`'s native-language search protocol — Keyword Compendium, direct Co-1/Tier-2/Co-2 publication-page retrieval in-language — is the primary tool, not this one.
   356	- Run citation-miner on non-English sources *after* multilingual-research (or another skill) has surfaced them, using the §2 non-DOI fetch-and-read path.

1	---
     2	name: research-log-manager
     3	description: >
     4	  SQLite-backed search log and Best Practices Compendium (BPC) manager. Three actions:
     5	  CHECK (query slug status from SQLite + load BPC from GitHub), LOG (write search results
     6	  to search-log file + update SQLite coverage), RETRIEVE (load BPC for item-specification-writer).
     7	  Uses per-slug topic-directory architecture. ALWAYS use before and after every
     8	  multilingual-research run. Trigger on: "CHECK slug", "LOG results", "RETRIEVE BPC",
     9	  "search status", "what do we know about", or any research workflow start/end.
    10	---
    11	
    12	**Model:** Sonnet-class (mechanical) · Opus-class or above (if BPC synthesis judgment needed)
    13	**GitHub backend:** `jordanelias/guidebook` · `main`
    14	**SQLite:** `data/guidebook.db` via `scripts/db.py`
    15	
    16	> **C2 overhaul 2026-05-05:** All register operations use SQLite and db.py CLI.
    17	> `slug-registry.md`, `gap_register.md`, and `citation-mining-register.md` are archived.
    18	> All slug lookups, coverage writes, and gap filings go through db.py subcommands.
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	## Slug Resolution (all actions)
    23	
    24	Query SQLite first:
    25	
    26	```bash
    27	python3 scripts/db.py coverage --slug {slug}
    28	```
    29	
    30	Returns: the (language, jurisdiction) pairs owed (pairs_required, from `v_research_scope`) and the ones still
    31	unsearched (pairs_unsearched), the searched counts, searches_outside_scope, the owed jurisdictions the declared
    32	vocabulary refuses (jurisdictions_unreachable), and `complete`, which is false while anything owed is unsearched.
    33	
    34	For slug → topic_directory lookup:
    35	```sql
    36	SELECT slug, topic_directory, sl_path, bpc_path, status
    37	FROM slugs WHERE slug = '{slug}'
    38	```
    39	
    40	**New slug:** INSERT into slugs table, create BPC + search-log files on GitHub, commit.
    41	
    42	---
    43	
    44	## CHECK action
    45	
    46	1. Query coverage:
    47	   ```bash
    48	   python3 scripts/db.py coverage --slug {slug}
    49	   ```
    50	2. GET BPC file from GitHub: `references/bpc/{topic_directory}/{slug}.md`
    51	3. Report to calling skill: jurisdictions searched/not searched, languages searched/not searched, evidence tier range, coverage gaps.
    52	
    53	**New slug:** report "No prior research. Starting fresh."
    54	
    55	---
    56	
    57	## LOG action
    58	
    59	After multilingual-research completes:
    60	
    61	1. **Update search-log file on GitHub:** Append search results, new sources, coverage data.
    62	
    63	2. **Log every search you ran — one row per query, verbatim (R8):**
    64	   ```bash
    65	   python3 scripts/db.py log-search \
    66	     --slug {slug} \                   # omit for a search made for one parameter (--parameter {parameter_id}) or one source (--mined-ref-id); a search naming none is refused
    67	     --language {lang_code} \
    68	     --jurisdiction {jur_code} \        # omit if the search was not jurisdiction-scoped
    69	     --identity {identity_code} --icf {icf_code} --needs {need_code} \   # the lens this query covered; each optional and checked against its registry (--medical once that registry has rows)
    70	     --query-text '{the query, exactly as fired}' \
    71	     --terms-used '["alias1","MeSH term","alias2"]' \   # JSON array — the column is json_valid-checked
    72	     --engine {pubmed|crossref|web|...} \
    73	     --depth-method {scoping|systematic} \             # only two; a citation chase is --mining-direction
    74	     --target-tier {1..6} --target-evidence-type {co1|clinical|code|...} \
    75	     --results-found {N} --results-screened {N} --results-admitted {N} \
    76	     --admitted-ref-id REF-NNNNN \      # repeatable; writes the admission junction too
    77	     --session {session_filename}
    78	   ```
    79	   Once per query. **Keep the empties** — a zero-yield search with a well-formed
    80	   query is a completed unit of work and evidence about the world (R8, R14).
